body:
# the contributor audit: paired maximum-depth equality rigidity, d>=3

Full source `candidate d494e7e71949ac0b` read.

Fradelizi-Guédon localization theorem as its external input.

The strictness argument uses one mean inequality, a compact interval,
and a convex upper semicontinuous sum of CLOSED lower-tail masses.
The attained extremizer theorem is essential and explicitly retained.
Admissible Dirac laws give at most1, below2-2Gamma. For nonconstant
decreasing affine powers, the reflected increasing CDF sum strictly
increases on the first proper-cut interval and is at least1 thereafter.
For increasing powers, the exact d3 factor gives positive gap
P(r)/(32(1+r+r²)^4), and the d>=4 quadrature gives gap at least53/3750.
Uniform laws are separate. Thus every actual maximizing extremizer is
strict at fixed positive shift; no nonattained strict family is used.
The mean and measure-concavity parameters of actual convex-body
marginals are tracked correctly. Atomlessness turns lower-tail bounds
into the desired closed upper-tail inequality.

The compact parameter set uses unit normals and bounded shifts. Its
continuous cap functional attains the infimum, and the maximum over K
exists. At equality every active shift is zero. Separation of the
compact active-normal hull supplies an actual inner-ball movement:
near active parameters BOTH cap thresholds decrease through sections
with uniformly positive area; away from them a compact mass gap and
an outer-ball slab bound apply. This proves balancing without a
derivative-envelope assumption.

The ordinary equality pyramids have distinct apices. Every other
extreme point lies in the respective base, which proves Kronecker
values of their affine heights at the chosen apices. A positive
balanced combination of height gradients is constant; evaluation at
apices forces equal coefficients, and averaging heights forces exactly
d+1 of them. The resulting barycentric constraints prove that K is
their simplex. The converse uses a facet-parallel cap at each point
and the already proved centroid pair bound.

The source explicitly excludes d2, where nonzero-shift equality occurs.
All steps concern ordinary bodies and supply no mixed-integer point.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
